blocks.content: Recognizing distractor options and avoiding negative marking traps is essential for maximizing rank in competitive examinations.

rows: Underline or highlight key constraint words immediately while reading the question.
Selecting the first option that looks familiar without reading all choices
Read all options completely before marking the answer sheet.
Spending excessive time on a lengthy or stubborn question
Use the skip-and-return approach to secure easy marks first.

items: Always scan for negative framing words like 'NOT', 'INCORRECT', and 'EXCEPT' before selecting an option.
Verify unit conversions (e.g., converting km/h to m/s) before finalizing numerical answers.
Never spend more than 60-90 seconds on a single question during the first attempt pass.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Exam traps heavily exploit negative marking by tempting candidates into making hasty, unverified guesses.
Overlooking critical qualifiers like 'NOT', 'INCORRECT', or 'EXCEPT' is the most frequent source of silly mistakes.
Distractor options are intentionally designed using common calculation errors or partial truths to mislead candidates.
Time-sink questions are placed strategically to create panic and reduce time available for easier questions.
